chapter: Thomas, own bands and neighborhood clubs
title: Leading his own band at Raceland and Grand Island
summary: After Thomas, Barnes ran a band for a dance hall owner near Raceland, at times fourteen pieces and two jobs, in the 1930s.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yeah. Same scene. When you see Thomas doesn't work hard in the band, you know. He's a little bit cool. He comes up strong all the time. He puts a car and takes a rest. You know, see, when he's playing. And I left from Thomas and I started waiting down to Grand Island. Which was Tony Marullo down there. Who's that now? Tony Marullo. You know him, Nick?
That's the guy that owned the place? Yeah.
Well whose band was it? My band.

Your own band. Who was in it? Well, that band then I had Harrison Brand and myself, and Puri, Psych, Buster, Harrison Cousins, Travmore. I had Mitchell Frazier, Piano. Who I had on the drummers, see. I don't remember who I had on the drummers. Well I know, but we hold that young guy for a long time.
You stayed down there?

No, I didn't stay down there. I just went down there and they had a wave on the Wednesday, come up on a Sunday morning, Monday morning. Then I run two bands. We had Miss LaVar at Grand Island and, not Grand Island, not, how do you call that? The room where you're touring is going.
Where what?
The room where you're touring is going to Grand Island. LaVar, 10 hours, a big dance hall there.
Is it near Raceland?
Raceland, yeah, at Raceland. That big dance hall is Raceland. Well I hold that down. We scripted a band and I hired other men.
Who played trumpet with you then?
Probably Pajol. Willie Pajol, Bob Anthony, those two trumpets. And I remember, I can't remember who I had with me. I had a 14 piece band all together that I cared.
14 pieces playing at once?

Yeah. I had two jobs. Oh, two different bands. I had to work at Grand Island and I had to work at the island. See? So between Tony and Mr. LaVar, they straightened out. You know, between them, that would work that way.
And you were collecting the leaders for both jobs? Yeah. Both jobs. Where did you play? Grand Island?
Well, Grand Island one time, I think, I had to split.
I see.
Yeah, I just had to split.
I see. Now, this is in the 30s I guess, Dick, huh? You up to the 30s yet or were you in the 20s? What would you think?
Was this after the Depression or?
No, this was in the, somewhere in the 30s or something. This is the 30s. This is after the Depression?
Yeah. We got out of the Depression. I see. Did you do any work in the Jitneys they had around here then? No, not here. Not here.

In town. I wouldn't play the Jitneys town, I would play Jitneys down there. Down there the Jitneys town was different, you see it was too hard. In the walls it was too hard. Yeah, it was too hard. Down there we had the dancers barricades, the dance hall. And we'd play a number, well I'd say a holy number. This would a crowd to get in and make a dance. And by the time the one to leave from here and go around and get back there and get stopped. Now we'd take a rest right then until the last one get out the ring. Last one then we'd pick up the gun. That's where we'd want to know both ends. Mr. Labot and Mr. Maloney they thought it was great the way I was massing the business, you know, because I'd watch it good. So they, you couldn't do nothing about it, he said, nothing to me. They had the crap game on one side and the crap game on one side. We're finding them right now, I guess they'd be short they could get, you know where I was they call them now. I don't know. In fact I know how them places is, what they look like.
Well I think they have a big dance hall at Raceland. Now they play rock and roll.
Oh the one time I played at Raceland with Thomas a couple years ago. Yeah at Raceland and they had the Hillbatter band there. Yeah. Yeah a Hillbatter band there.
